# A const whose initializer reads itself does not take the compiler down.
#
# `evalIdent` reads a const's value by evaluating its initializer, and the
# initializer reads the const: evalIdent <-> evalExpr with nothing between
# them. `const a int = a` was a one-line program that ended in
#
#   runtime: goroutine stack exceeds 1000000000-byte limit
#   fatal error: stack overflow
#
# with no position and no message. Pre-existing, and found from the other end:
# the identical shape in a window prop (window_prop_reads_itself.txt) needed
# the same guard, keyed the same way, twenty lines away.
#
# Answered "not constant", which leaves the initializer standing -- what a
# const the optimizer cannot evaluate already does. That is survivable rather
# than right: the page below carries no value for `a`, silently. The rule that
# a declaration may not read itself belongs in the checker, where it reaches a
# program this pass never folds; CLAUDE.md says so and this fixture is what
# changing it would update.
#
# A CLI script rather than a golden because what is asserted is that the
# compiler comes back at all.
sngl generate --lang none --platform html --out out selfconst.sngl
grep '<title>t</title>' out/index.html

# A cycle reaches the guard by a second key rather than the first one twice.
sngl generate --lang none --platform html --out out2 cycle.sngl
grep '<title>t</title>' out2/index.html

-- selfconst.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

const a int = a

window #home(title="t", href="/index.html") {
    text(value="{a}")
}
-- cycle.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

const a int = b
const b int = a

window #home(title="t", href="/index.html") {
    text(value="{a}")
}
